VERIFICATION PASS (2026-11-04)

What was checked:
- All 32 entries were re-checked against the primary sources:
  - 28 arXiv papers via the HTML pages or, where there is no HTML, the PDF.
  - 4 CVF open-access PDFs: UniVAD, Zhang CVPR24, FPDM, and the MULDE/EVAL/STG-NF listings.
- Pages were downloaded with curl and parsed cell by cell, not through a summarising fetch model.
- Verification copies are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lei-Desktop-msc/e8dc9422-76c8-42e7-babd-ff39d7dc137d/scratchpad/vsota/html and /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lei-Desktop-msc/e8dc9422-76c8-42e7-babd-ff39d7dc137d/scratchpad/vsota/pdf. The VLAVAD table image is in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lei-Desktop-msc/e8dc9422-76c8-42e7-babd-ff39d7dc137d/scratchpad/vsota/img.
- No repo files were modified.

Results:
- All papers exist, and no entry was deleted.
- Every headline AUC value matched its source table.
- 19 entries are confirmed and 13 corrected. The corrections are mostly in metadata and protocol notes.

Corrections that change numbers or venues:
- AccI-VAD fps: null -> 12. The paper reports 12 FPS on an RTX 2080 with an average of 5 objects per frame.
- MLLM-EVAD: venue is TMLR, year changed 2025 -> 2026 (official TMLR bib).
- MS2CAST: the Avenue coefficient is w=0.9, not 1.0.
- VADMamba: 14.84M / 28.21M are FP-branch parameter counts only; the hybrid model also has an FR branch.
- AnyAnomaly: author list fixed.

Claims in the earlier notes that the papers did not support:
- 'Strictly causal' paper: the claim that ShT was 'partly obtained'.
- YOLO-pose+CLIP: the claim that the paper 'states no Jetson-class device tested'.
- TrajVAD: the claim that it is 'standardised with training statistics'.
- SAAF: the 'frame-centric' label on its MULDE 81.40 row.
- Zhang CVPR24: the 'YOLOv3' detector.
- STNMamba: 'per-video' normalisation; the scope is not stated.
- MoG-VLM: the claim that the ShT split is unstated. The paper describes 107 test videos, the standard one-class test split.

New caveat for AccI-VAD: its Table 2 ShT pair (85.9 micro / 89.6 macro) mixes two feature configurations. 85.9 is Pose+Velocity, whose macro is 88.8. 89.6 is all three features, whose micro is 85.1.

WHICH FAMILIES LEAD (strict one-class, micro AUC, standard splits):
- UCSD Ped2 is saturated:
  - MULDE 99.7 and DMAD 99.7 (density / memory).
  - Then the bi-directional hybrid 99.3, AccI-VAD 99.1 and VLAVAD 99.0.
  - Most methods sit at 95-99. MM-VAD's 98.81 is a training-free protocol outlier.
- CUHK Avenue is led by object-centric methods:
  - MULDE 94.3.
  - Then AccI-VAD 93.7, HSC with motion augmentation 93.7 and SSMTL++v1 93.7.
  - Then Zhang CVPR24∗ 93.6.
  - HSC's 93.7 uses pseudo-abnormal motion augmentation. Zhang's 94.3 needs virtual-anomaly training.
- ShanghaiTech is led by object, pose, trajectory and multi-stream models:
  - UniVAD (WACV 2026): 89.3, or 89.5 with per-dataset tuning.
  - TrajVAD-P (ECCV 2026): 88.6.
  - VLAVAD (arXiv only): 87.2.
  - Zhang CVPR24∗: 86.8.
  - MULDE: 86.7.
  - DA-Flow: 86.5.
  - STG-NF and AccI-VAD: 85.9; RPC: 85.89.
- LLM/VLM methods:
  - AnomalyRuler (few-shot normal references, GPT-4 induction) reaches 85.2 on ShT.
  - LAVIDA reaches 85.28, but it is trained on external pseudo-anomalies.
  - Strictly zero-shot, training-free methods score lower: AnyAnomaly 79.7, SAAF 80.54, MoG-VLM 78.96.

TYPICAL BANDS:
- Frame-centric prediction / Mamba / diffusion (STNMamba 2024, VADMamba, MA-PDM, MS2CAST): Ped2 96.1-98.6, Avenue 85.8-91.5, ShT 74.9-79.2.
  - The TIP 2024 bi-directional hybrid is an outlier at 82.2 on ShT.
- Object / pose / trajectory / multi-stream: ShT about 85.9-89.3.
- Zero-shot / few-shot VLM-LLM:
  - Avenue 87.3-89.7; ShT 78.96-85.3.
  - Speed ranges from about 0.6 FPS (MM-VAD, 1.69 s/frame) and 1.36 FPS (AnyAnomaly with MiniCPM-V) to 33-40 FPS amortized (SAAF, MoG-VLM on an A100; AnyAnomaly with vLLM and Qwen2.5-VL-3B: 34.78).
  - Models used are about 3-17B parameters.
- Causal or very light designs:
  - The strictly-causal SSM falls far below: 67.9 Ped2 / 70.2 Avenue.
  - YOLO-pose+CLIP is competitive on Avenue (89.26) but low on ShT (70.26). It is not causal, because it applies Gaussian smoothing.

EFFICIENCY (all GPU numbers come from the papers' own tables):
- High-FPS methods are all frame-level, at 78-79 on ShT:
  - AED-MAE (CVPR24): 1655 FPS, 3M params, 0.8 GFLOPs.
  - Fast-AED (CVIU24): 1480 FPS, about 5M params, 6.2 GFLOPs; 88 FPS on an Intel i9 CPU.
- Other measured speeds:
  - STG-NF: about 1K params, 189 FPS, plus an 83M-param pose front-end.
  - VideoPatchCore: 96.1 FPS on ShT (RTX 3090).
  - Bi-directional hybrid: 94 FPS (A5000).
  - VADMamba: 90 FPS (GPU not named).
  - STNMamba: 40 FPS (Titan XP).
  - SSMTL++: about 20 FPS.
  - AccI-VAD: 12 FPS (RTX 2080).
- None of the papers checked reports results on a Jetson, Raspberry Pi, NPU or phone. The closest are:
  - an Apple M3 Pro via MPS (the strictly-causal paper);
  - an i9 CPU (Fast-AED);
  - about 10 FPS per feed on five live CCTV feeds (YOLO-pose+CLIP; hardware for this not stated).
  - STNMamba only claims edge-deployment 'potential'.

PROTOCOL CAVEATS:
1. Macro AUC is consistently higher than micro. AccI-VAD ShT is 85.9 vs 89.6 (mixed configurations, see above); MULDE is 86.7 vs 91.5.
2. Several papers min-max normalise scores in a way that needs future frames:
   - VADMamba Eq. 8 (over t within a video).
   - The strictly-causal SSM ('per clip'), despite its name.
   - STNMamba and the bi-directional hybrid use min-max with unstated scope.
   - Contours normalises its input features at video level.
3. Temporal smoothing is common, and the papers do not say whether it is causal: AccI-VAD, VideoPatchCore, VLAVAD, VADMamba, Contours, YOLO-pose+CLIP (sigma=5), MLLM-EVAD (studied in its appendix), AnomalyRuler (majority vote with padding 5). The bi-directional hybrid needs up to 12 future frames.
4. Some methods add supervision, pseudo-anomalies or per-dataset tuning:
   - Pseudo-anomalies or external data: Zhang CVPR24 ▽ (virtual data), HSC MA (motion augmentation), AED-MAE (synthetic UBnormal anomalies), LAVIDA (external segmentation data).
   - AnomalyRuler uses 10 normal shots plus GPT-4.
   - Per-dataset weights or coefficients: UniVAD†, VideoPatchCore, MS2CAST (w), AnyAnomaly (gamma1-3).
5. Detectors in use:
   - Mask R-CNN: AccI-VAD.
   - YOLOv3: SSMTL++, HSC, Fast-AED teachers.
   - YOLOv5: VideoPatchCore, UniVAD.
   - YOLOv7 with BoT-SORT: Contours.
   - YOLOX: STG-NF, DA-Flow, TrajVAD.
   - YOLOv11n-pose: YOLO-pose+CLIP.
   - AlphaPose for the pose-based methods.
6. Baselines are reported inconsistently across papers:
   - AccI-VAD appears as 76.2 on ShT in AnyAnomaly, which is exactly MULDE's frame-centric AccI-VAD-GMM reimplementation. YOLO-pose+CLIP lists it at 86.0 / 71.1. Its own numbers are 93.7 / 85.9.
   - MULDE appears as 81.40 (SAAF, setting unstated), 81.3 (its own frame-centric) or 86.7 (its own object-centric).
7. Some training-free VLM papers probably use a different ShT split, likely the weakly supervised one: MM-VAD (ShT 96.95, LAVAD 94.55) and the 'Yu Wang et al.' 98.13 row in MoG-VLM's table. Do not compare these with one-class numbers.
8. 'Look Inside Each Video' (arXiv 2608.21854, Table 4): on ShT only 0.814% of anomalous-normal frame pairs come from the same video, so micro-AUROC is close to Cross-AUROC. Video-mean replacement, which sets Within-AUROC to 50%, drops micro-AUROC sharply: TrajVAD-P from 88.59 to 61.92 and UniVAD from 89.32 to 61.30. That argues for also reporting macro or within-video AUROC.

EXCLUDED OR NOT TABLED (from the earlier pass; not re-verified here):
- VADSK (arXiv 2503.10653): reported as a supervised classifier trained on test-set frames.
- TAO (CVPR 2025): pixel / RBDC / TBDC only.
- GridVAD: Ped2 pixel AUROC only.
- Probe-VAD, CSI-VAD, QVAD, TD-VAD, LaGoVAD: no Ped2, Avenue or ShT frame AUC.
- Bameri (IET 2025): weakly supervised.

Venues taken only from arXiv comments and not yet visible in proceedings: MoG-VLM (BMVC 2026), SAAF (WACV 2027), LAVIDA (CVPR 2026).

Verification pass (2026-11-04). All 29 entries are real papers and none are duplicates, so none were deleted. Each was re-checked against the primary source:
- arXiv PDFs were downloaded and searched with pdftotext.
- IEEE Xplore and Wiley blocked curl with a bot-check, so their full text, plus the SRAE PDF, was read in the built-in browser. Key IEEE table images (SwinAnomaly T3, MsMp-net T3, Guo T3, Hong T11, SYRFA T1, Kasegn T7) were cropped and viewed directly.
- Venues and DOIs came from CrossRef and OpenAlex.
- No repo files were touched.
Result: 14 confirmed, 15 corrected, 0 unverifiable.

Venue corrections. Seven entries listed as arXiv-only or 'venue not stated' are now published:
- STNMamba: IEEE TMM 2026.
- M2S2L: IEEE VCIP 2025.
- ABAE: Knowledge-Based Systems 2026.
- Light-WVAD: Neurocomputing 2025.
- YOLO-CLIP: IEEE MIPR 2026.
- DA-Flow: IEEE TMM 2025.
- OMAE: ICIP 2022.
Numbers for these were checked against the arXiv versions only.

Newly read full texts (previously gaps):
- AONet: 29 FPS on a Tesla V100. Its own Table 4 lists a baseline at 32 FPS, which contradicts its 'matching or exceeding' claim.
- SRAE: Ped2 95.41, Avenue 80.9, 4.8M params, 1.6 GFLOPs, no FPS.
- Kasegn Table 7: Ped1 83.12, Ped2 84.39, Avenue 85.88, SHT 84.92. Table 5 (params/FLOPs) is still unread.

New unfavourable findings:
- **VADMamba:** the hybrid 98.5 / 91.5 / 77.0 relies on Eq. 9. For each test video it keeps the frame or flow score with the higher AUC on that video, which uses ground-truth labels (oracle selection).
- **Honnegowda et al.:** uses UCSD Ped1, not Ped2, as the paper states explicitly.
- **YOLO-CLIP:** reports Avenue and SHT AUC identical to its baseline despite different scoring. Its baseline detector is described inconsistently (YOLO vs Mask R-CNN).
- **Kasegn:** reports 4,020 Ped2 test frames; the standard set has 2,010.
- **CASRE:** the Ped2 test set has only 14 clips.
- **FastAno:** SD-MAE Table 5 gives FastAno 64M params / 84 GFLOPs, against 2.15M in FastAno's own text.
- **Per-video or test-set normalization** (min/max or max of scores) is used by FastAno, AONet, Kobayashi, VADMamba, ABAE, M2S2L, Hong and MsMp-net.

(1) Embedded-device results:
- 0 of 29 papers report a measured result on a named embedded device (Jetson, Raspberry Pi, FPGA, phone or NPU).
- CPU-only throughput on desktop or server CPUs appears in 3 papers: Lightning KD (88 FPS, Intel i9), SwinAnomaly (1.96 fps, i7) and Kasegn (354 FPS, Xeon Gold 6248). Dilek & Dener's CPU-vs-GPU Table 21 was not read.
- Edge suitability is claimed without measurement by STNMamba, SRAE, Kasegn, CASRE and YOLO-CLIP (as future work).
- A measured Jetson or Raspberry Pi result on these benchmarks would still be a real point of difference.

(2) How speed is reported.

**Hardware varies widely.**
- RTX 3090: 4 timing papers (FastAno, SD-MAE, Lightning, Hong). SD-MAE and Lightning print it as 'GTX 3090'.
- Titan Xp / TITAN X: 4 (STG-NF, STNMamba, YOLO-CLIP, OMAE).
- GTX 1080Ti: 2 (SSMTL; MsMp-net as training environment).
- RTX 2080Ti: 3 (MULDE, CASRE; Kobayashi, development only).
- One each: A5000, 4090, 3070, 2060/3080, A100, Tesla M10, Tesla V100 (AONet), RTX 3060 (SRAE, no timing), GTX 1070Ti (Honnegowda), RTX 3080 (DA-Flow, no timing).
- No GPU named: VADMamba and M2S2L give FPS; SPARTA gives latency.

**Batch size is almost never stated.** SwinAnomaly shows why it matters: 4.32 fps per stream vs 107 fps batched with 2 s latency.

**Detector, flow and pose time:**
- Counted in the timing: Guo et al. (0.0375 s/frame incl. YOLOv3 + SelFlow), YOLO-CLIP (51.39 FPS incl. decoding and transfer), and SSMTL, whose 23/21 FPS includes YOLOv3 per Sec 6.2. The earlier 'ambiguous' label for SSMTL is corrected.
- VADMamba includes 'data processing and anomaly score calculation', but FlowNet2 is not mentioned.
- The pose estimator appears excluded: STG-NF; unclear for SPARTA.
- Hong et al. need DeepLabv3 + FlowNet2 at test time, and inclusion is not stated.
- OMAE lists pre-processing separately: about 260 ms per frame vs 20 ms per batch of 256.
- MULDE's 25 FPS uses a different backbone (Hiera-Base) than its accuracy figure (Hiera-L).
- The Bi-directional TIP model has a built-in 12-frame look-ahead (0.40 s at 30 FPS).

**Baseline FPS sources differ, and the earlier claim needs nuance.**
- SD-MAE and Lightning state that all baseline FPS were re-measured on their own GTX 3090.
- MsMp-net explicitly copies baseline times.
- STNMamba mixes collected and reproduced values while saying all ran on a TITAN XP.
- VADMamba does not say.
- So MNAD's 101 (SD-MAE, 3090), 65 (STNMamba, TITAN XP; also copied by M2S2L) and 78 (VADMamba, unstated) partly reflect different hardware.
- SSMTL: 21 FPS on a 1080Ti in its own paper vs 51 FPS on a 3090 in SD-MAE.

**Accuracy protocol is often mixed.** SSMTL's 99.8 / 92.8 / 90.2 equal the macro values in SD-MAE Table 1; the micro values are 97.5 / 91.5 / 82.4.

Efficiency frontier (unchanged, re-verified):
- **Fastest:** SD-MAE (3M params, 0.8 GFLOPs, 1655 FPS; micro 95.4 / 91.3 / 79.1) and Lightning KD (5M params, 6.2 GFLOPs, 1480 FPS; micro 95.9 / 88.3 / 78.4).
- **Smallest:** pose models at about 0.5K-1K params (STG-NF, DA-Flow), excluding the pose estimator.
- **Mamba models:** 40-90 FPS with 7-28M params, at Ped2 98.0-98.5, Avenue 89-92, SHT 75-78. VADMamba's hybrid AUC is oracle-fused, as noted above.

(3) IEEE Access accuracy band, 2023-2026 (papers' own numbers, all re-verified):
- Standard one-class, frame-level protocol:
  - Ped2: 96.7-98.2 (Niaz 96.7, SYRFA 96.9, Kobayashi 97.5, MsMp-net 97.6, Guo 97.9, SwinAnomaly 98.2, Hong 98.2).
  - Avenue: 84.7-91.2 (Niaz 84.7, SwinAnomaly 84.8, Guo 86.7, MsMp-net 89.0, Hong 91.2).
  - ShanghaiTech, frame-based models: 74.8-76.5 (Niaz 74.8, SwinAnomaly 76.3, Hong 76.5).
  - ShanghaiTech reaches about 84.6-85.8 only with extra cues: synthetic supervision + YOLOv3 (SYRFA 84.6), pose (SPARTA 85.75), or per-video max-normalized prediction (Kobayashi 85.8).
  - So IEEE Access frame-based papers sit at or a little below the top-venue frontier (about 98.5 / 91-92 / 77-78 for the 2025 Mamba models; SD-MAE micro 95.4 / 91.3 / 79.1).
- Several of these carry protocol caveats: SwinAnomaly computes AUC from binary labels with per-dataset tuned thresholds; Hong uses dataset-specific score weights and an implied sliding-window AUC.
- IEEE Access has also accepted weak or non-standard evaluations:
  - Kasegn 2026: Ped2 AUC 84.39, with the paper framing its contribution as 354 FPS on CPU.
  - Dilek & Dener 2024: 100% Ped2 after abnormal test frames were moved into training, then random frame splits.
  - CASRE 2026: clip-level accuracy on 14 Ped2 test clips.
  - SwinAnomaly 2023: AUC from binary predictions.
- 9 of 11 IEEE Access papers report some efficiency metric; SYRFA and Kobayashi do not.
- **Practical bar:** competitive but not state-of-the-art accuracy, for example Ped2 ≥ 97, Avenue about 85-91 and SHT about 75-77 for frame-level methods, together with a clearly measured efficiency contribution. A properly documented end-to-end or embedded measurement would exceed what any IEEE Access VAD paper surveyed here reports.

Verification summary (2026-11-04): all 93 entries are real sources and every numeric value matched its source. No entries were deleted. 26 entries are 'corrected' and the rest 'confirmed'. Most corrections only remove labels that the source does not state:
- 'INT8' removed on the Hailo Model Zoo tables, the Hailo community post and the Coral pages.
- 'PyTorch' removed on NeuFlow v1.
- 'via DeepStream' removed on the DeepStream-guide table.
- The rknn precision note was rewritten using the v8.3.152 exporter source.
- Two Raspberry Pi 5 price entries: the brief at the cited URL is now 'Published November 2026'.
- The Hailo community column label was fixed.
No repo files were modified. Raw sources were downloaded only to the scratchpad (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-lei-Desktop-msc/e8dc9422-76c8-42e7-babd-ff39d7dc137d/scratchpad/src).

Board recommendation, based only on the numbers found:
NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super looks most suitable for >=10 FPS, and Jetson Orin NX 16GB is equivalent or slightly faster. Among the sources collected, Orin is the only platform family with published numbers for all three heavy neural stages:
- Detector: YOLO11n TensorRT FP16 is 4.53 ms on the Orin Nano Super and 4.73 ms on the Orin NX 16GB (Ultralytics 8.3.157; pre- and post-processing excluded).
- Learned dense flow: NeuFlow v2 runs at 'over 20 FPS' at 512x384 on the original (pre-Super) Orin Nano 8GB. It takes 0.106 s at Sintel 1024x436 with half-precision models.
- CLIP-class ViT embedding: ViT-B/32 runs at 314 FPS on the Orin Nano Super and 356.7 FPS on the Orin NX 16GB (FP16 TensorRT; batch size and resolution not stated).
- My own arithmetic, not a measurement: detector plus flow at 512x384 is roughly 4.5 ms plus less than 50 ms, which leaves room under a 100 ms budget. This mixes devices: the detector number is from the Orin Nano Super, while the NeuFlow v2 number is from the original Orin Nano, which should be slower. It also excludes pre-/post-processing, tracking and scoring.
- Flow is the dominant cost, so flow resolution must stay at or below about 512x384. NeuFlow v2 at Sintel resolution is about 9.4 FPS on its own (my arithmetic: 1/0.106 s).
- Not published (in the sources found): YOLO11n-pose on Jetson, MobileCLIP2-S0 on Jetson, and any measurement of this project's full pipeline on any edge board.
- The VPI hardware optical flow accelerator (OFA) on Jetson AGX Orin takes 2.93 ms at 1080p with grid 4, which is block-level flow. NVIDIA's VPI 4.1 docs name only 'Jetson AGX Orin and Thor devices' for OFA, and the perf table lists only those two devices, so OFA on Orin Nano/NX is unconfirmed.

Unfavourable findings for the other boards:
- **Raspberry Pi 5 CPU:**
  - YOLO11n alone takes 94.03 ms (NCNN) or 84.76 ms (OpenVINO), from Ultralytics 8.3.152. YOLO26n NCNN takes 67.03 ms (8.4.108).
  - The detector alone uses up most of the 100 ms budget, so >=10 FPS for the full pipeline is not supported.
  - Ultralytics' two YOLO11n ONNX figures on the Pi 5 disagree: 191.09 ms (8.3.152) and 147.20 ms (8.4.14).
  - The repo's earlier Raspberry Pi 4 result was 1.4-1.9 FPS, which I checked in HANDOFF.md at lines 229 and 304.
- **Raspberry Pi 5 + Hailo-8L/8:**
  - Detector and pose are fast in the Model Zoo: yolov11n runs at 157 (8L) and 185 (8) FPS at batch size 1, and yolov8s_pose at 107 (8L) and 393 (8) FPS.
  - The zoo tables were measured on an Intel i5-9400 host over PCIe Gen3 x4. The Pi 5 link is single-lane, which the Hailo community post states. The community Pi 5 numbers are at batch size 8 (yolov8s 127.85, yolov8s_pose 123.43; FPS implied, no unit given). The poster is not flagged as Hailo staff.
  - The Hailo-8L pose list has no yolo11n-pose: only centerpose_regnetx_800mf, yolov8m_pose and yolov8s_pose.
  - CLIP-family encoders are slow at batch size 1: TinyCLIP-40M/32 runs at 35.2 FPS (8L) and 38.0 FPS (8), and ViT-B/32 at 30.0 FPS (8L). Per-object crop embedding would break 10 FPS once there are several objects per frame unless crops are batched (98.6 and 186 FPS at batch size 8 for TinyCLIP-40M/32).
  - I found no optical flow model or MobileCLIP in the Hailo zoo tables checked. This was not exhaustively checked across all task pages.
  - The Model Zoo tables do not state bit-width.
- **RK3588:**
  - At INT8 on a single NPU core, yolo11n runs at 64.0 FPS and yolov8n-pose at 58.3 FPS (max NPU frequency, model inference only).
  - The CLIP ViT-B/32 image encoder runs at only 6.9 FPS (FP16), so embedding is the bottleneck, and there are no flow numbers.
  - Ultralytics' Rock 5B YOLO11n figure (71.5 ms, a non-quantized RKNN build in 8.3.152) is far slower than the RKNN zoo INT8 figure.
  - Ultralytics' YOLO26n INT8 figure (41.2 ms) is flagged by Ultralytics as to be refreshed. Its INT8 accuracy was validated only in the rknn-toolkit2 simulator.
- **Coral Edge TPU:** The only figures are YOLOv8n at 320 (22.2 ms standard, 16.7 ms high-frequency, on a Pi 5 8GB with a USB Coral) and classic CNNs. There are no flow or CLIP numbers.
- **IMX500 (Raspberry Pi AI Camera):** YOLO11n takes 58.82 ms and YOLO11n-pose 62.50 ms. Alone that is about 17 and 16 FPS, below 20 FPS (my arithmetic). The pose mAP was measured on COCO8-Pose, which has only 8 images.

Components with no published edge numbers found (search coverage, not proof of absence):
- YOLO11n-pose on Jetson, Pi 5 CPU, Hailo or RK3588. Only the IMX500 has it. The proxies are yolov8s_pose on Hailo and yolov8n-pose on RK3588.
- RAFT-small on any edge device. There is full RAFT on the Orin Nano: 1.060 s at 32 iters (half precision, NeuFlow v2 paper) and 0.760 s at 12 iters (mixed precision disabled, NeuFlow v1 paper), both on Sintel. There is also RAFT-Large with TensorRT on the Xavier NX: 128.16 ms for 5 extractions, and 26.64 ms for a single inference per the paper's text. RAFT-Small is mentioned only qualitatively.
- OpenCV DIS on any edge board.
- NeuFlow v1/v2 on Orin NX, Orin Nano Super, Pi 5, Hailo or RK3588. Only the original Orin Nano has numbers.
- MobileCLIP and MobileCLIP2 S0/S1. Only Apple's iPhone 12 Pro Max Core ML numbers exist (S0 image encoder 1.5 ms).
- DINOv2-small. Only DINOv2-base on Jetson.
- EfficientViT-B on edge, except the 'Orin' (Jetson AGX Orin) and 'Nano' columns in the paper.
- MobileNetV4 on boards. Only phone numbers exist, such as Pixel 8 EdgeTPU, which is not Coral.
- The Bayesian density scorer.

End-to-end VAD on edge boards:
- Pham et al. (FICC 2024, arXiv 2307.16834): RTFM with ResNet50-I3D features, which is weakly supervised and not object-centric. It reaches 47.56 FPS on the Orin Nano 8GB (15W) with Torch-TensorRT and 36.02 FPS without it. Its AUC is 84.39% on UCF-Crime and 88.4% on UIT-VNAnomaly.
- Huang, Wang, Hsu (IEEE Embedded Systems Letters 18(3):178-181, 2026; DOI 10.1109/LES.2025.3618635): a skeleton VAD pipeline (YOLOv8n-Pose, BoT-SORT and a normalizing-flow/MS-STGCN scorer) deployed on a Raspberry Pi 5. AUC is 86.2% on ShanghaiTech and 72.2% on UBnormal (unsupervised), and 82.4% on UBnormal (supervised). Its FPS was not accessible.
- No object-centric detector + pose + flow + embedding + density pipeline has been found measured on an edge board.
- The closest is Warnasooriya et al. (MIPR 2026, arXiv 2608.31074; YOLO11n-pose + CLIP ViT-B/32): 51.39 FPS, against 15.32 FPS for a Reiss & Hoshen-style baseline, both on a desktop Titan XP.
  - Its proposed Avenue and ShanghaiTech AUROCs (89.26 and 70.26) are identical to the baseline's in Table I, marked as sharing the same detector and evaluation.
  - The paper contradicts itself on the baseline detector: Mask R-CNN in Sec. V-D, 'YOLO-based detection' in the footnote.
- RuleVAD (arXiv 2410.21991) states it is 'fully deployable on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano board'. I searched the PDF text and found no measured Jetson FPS or latency.

Caveats:
